text.p: Gold was slightly easier on Wednesday and base metal prices were in comfortable ranges in subdued activity ahead of next week's Christmas holidays.
New York precious metals futures ended firm Wednesday, on moderate volumes, with sentiment seen improving after 12 days of consolidation near the year's lows.
COMEX February gold closed up 80 cents at $371.30 an ounce, on total estimated volume of 20,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $369.10/369.60, against the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $368.70, and up
from the New York close Tuesday at $368.40/368.80.

Copper prices picked up to finish near the day's highs comfortably above the $2,100 level on Wednesday, boosted by a widening backwardation, traders said. Three-months copper finished the afternoon kerb on the London Metal Exchange (LME) at $2,114, up $19 from Tuesday and right up against the day's high of $2,115. Business was patchy ahead of the Christmas holidays and traders said they expected copper to remain within its recent range barring unexpected news or surprise LME stock movements.
Aluminium also ticked higher on the back of copper, building on slightly stronger levels achieved on Tuesday. It finished at $1,537, also near the day's highs, and up $7 from Tuesday.
Nickel continued a steady recovery from the 26-month lows touched on Monday. It was last near its highs for the day at $6,640, up $65.
Tin ended just $10 lower at $5,820 after easing following Tuesday's hefty bounce from 19-month lows hit on Monday.
Zinc was little changed at $1,053, down $2, while lead eased back below the $700 level to end $3 weaker at $698.
Alloy was last bid at $1,370, up $5.

NYMEX crude broke its post-Gulf War high of $26.10 a barrel Wednesday afternoon after a spate of technical buying lifted crude out of lower levels late session. January crude hit $26.15 a barrel minutes before the market's close at 1510 EST, and rose as high as $26.20 a barrel, up 49 cents. In the morning, prompt crude failed to break $26.10, hit on October 22, sending it down to a session low of $25.03. With the January contract in crude expiring Thursday, dealers said tomorrow's price action in crude will determine whether this was a genuine technical breakout.

CBOT wheat futures closed mixed but mostly higher on concern about the extent of losses to Argentina's wheat crop and on cold weather in the U.S. winter wheat growing region, traders said. Recent heavy rainfall in Argentina destroyed nearly one half million acres of wheat and harmed the quality of up to one million tonnes, an Argentine government official said. But a grain trade source in Buenos Aires disagreed.
December closed lower on liquidation before expiration.
Wheat closed seven cents per bushel higher to 2-1/2 lower, with Dec down 2-1/2 at $4.02 and March up 6-1/2 at $4.00-3/4.
